sections.title: 2:3.YY4.4 Messages
2:3.YY4.4.1.1 Trigger Events
sections.extract: {{ provideVHLDescription.valueMarkdown}} A VHL Holder initiates the Provide VHL transaction when: The VHL Holder wishes to grant access to their health documents to a VHL Receiver The VHL Holder has obtained a valid VHL from a VHL Sharer (via ITI-YY3 Generate VHL transaction) The VHL Holder encounters a VHL Receiver capable of processing VHLs in a relevant healthcare context

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.4.1.2 Message Semantics
sections.extract: The VHL payload structure is defined in ITI-YY3 and aligns with the SMART Health Links specification. QR Code Transmission The VHL is transmitted via QR code with the following characteristics: VHL encoded as HCERT QR code with HC1: prefix Suitable for in-person encounters, walk-in clinics, emergency departments QR code contains HCERT/CWT structure with embedded VHL payload Can be displayed on screen or printed on

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.4.1.3 Expected Actions - VHL Holder
sections.extract: QR Code Transmission: The VHL Holder SHALL: 1. Verify QR code validity (not expired, CWT signature valid) 2. Display QR code on device screen or provide printed copy 3. Ensure QR code is displayed at appropriate size for reliable scanning 4. Provide passcode out-of-band if VHL is passcode-protected (P flag present) Verifiable Credential Transmission (VC Enveloped VHL Option): When the VHL Sharer supports the VC

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.4.2.1 Trigger Events
sections.extract: The VHL Receiver MAY provide optional acknowledgment to VHL Holder confirming receipt and validation. This is transmission-mechanism dependent.

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.4.2.2 Message Semantics
sections.extract: For transmission mechanisms supporting bidirectional communication, response MAY include: Element; Cardinality; Description Acknowledgment; 0..1; Confirmation VHL received and validated Receipt Identifier; 0..1; Unique identifier for receipt transaction Receiver Identifier; 0..1; Identifier of VHL Receiver organization Timestamp; 0..1; ISO 8601 timestamp of receipt {: .grid}

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.4.2.3 Expected Actions
sections.extract: VHL Receiver: MAY send acknowledgment if supported SHALL NOT include sensitive health information VHL Holder: MAY receive and store receipts SHALL NOT rely on acknowledgment for security decisions

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.5.1 VHL Integrity and Authenticity
sections.extract: Digital signature ensures VHL issued by trusted VHL Sharer VHL Receivers SHALL verify COSE signatures before trusting content CWT signature provides end-to-end trust verification

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.5.2 VHL Confidentiality
sections.extract: VHL does NOT contain PHI VHL only contains reference (URL) to retrieve documents Actual documents retrieved over secure channel (ITI-YY5)

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.5.3 Replay Attacks
sections.extract: VHL Sharers SHOULD include expiration timestamps in both CWT and VHL payload VHL Receivers SHOULD enforce expiration validation VHL Sharers MAY implement single-use VHLs Short expiration times reduce replay attack window

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.5.4 Passcode Protection
sections.extract: Passcode communicated out-of-band (not in VHL) "P" flag indicates passcode required Passcode validated during manifest retrieval (ITI-YY5 Part 2) VHL Sharers SHOULD implement rate limiting on passcode attempts

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.5.5 Trust Network Validation
sections.extract: VHL Receivers SHALL: Validate VHL Sharer is current participant in trust network Retrieve DSC from trust list using kid from CWT protected header Check certificate revocation status where applicable Reject VHLs from untrusted participants

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.5.6 QR Code Security
sections.extract: QR Code Characteristics: Can be photographed/copied - use time-limited expiration Suitable for supervised encounters (in-person, on-screen display) Digital signature provides authenticity verification Recommended for higher security scenarios Best Practices: Include short expiration times in CWT exp claim Use passcode protection (P flag) for sensitive data Display QR codes in controlled environments Avoid printing

sections.title: 2:3.YY4.5.7 VC Enveloped VHL Option Security
sections.extract: When the VHL is carried as a Verifiable Credential: The DataIntegrityProof SHALL chain to a trust anchor in the trust list (same framework used for CWT/HCERT verification) The VC expirationDate and the VHL payload's exp SHALL both be honored — VHL Receivers SHALL reject if either has passed Confidentiality is equivalent to the QR form: the VC carries the decryption key and MUST be treated as sensitive VHL Sharers
